claim_summary: HeraldLight contributes temporal queue and arrival-guided signal-duration control with critic-guided LLM action correction and workflow learning.

claim_evidence.quote: This paper presents HeraldLight, a dual LLMs architecture driven by Herald guided prompts. The LLM-Agent, enhanced via LoRA-based imitation fine-tuning, infers the active signal phase and duration from real-time traffic conditions.

modules.name: Queue and approaching-vehicle duration guidance
modules.scope_reason: Computes phase-specific signal durations from queues and approaching vehicles. R3_1 TSK applies because the output is the task's control duration; changing task family changes its objective and action space. Counterfactually, despite temporal inputs, this is not task-independent GTS temporal data handling.

evidence.quote: Herald Module determines signal phase durations by combining a queue-based release time model with predicted arrivals of running vehicles.

modules.name: Herald-guided phase-control interface
modules.scope_reason: The structured prompt specifies the traffic-control context, objective, constraints and output. R3_1 TSK applies because the interface embeds the phase-and-duration action format. Counterfactually, another task needs a different objective and output schema; it is not task-independent GTS handling.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - embeds signal phase and duration outputs

evidence.quote: The phase selection prompt is a structured template composed of six blocks: dintersection (static geometry and lane–phase mapping), dtask (objectives: phase choice and duration setting), ddetails (computational rules), dreq (I/O constraints and formatting), drules (fallbacks for edge cases), and dimportant (priority constraints to enforce consistency).

modules.name: Dual-LLM action correction
modules.scope_reason: The critic evaluates, corrects and scores signal-control actions. R3_1 TSK applies because correctness is judged against the phase-and-duration control task. Counterfactually, a different task changes action semantics and verifier; this is not task-independent GTS handling.

evidence.quote: a dual LLMs architecture is adopted: LLMAgent generates actions; LLM-Critic (a stronger reasoner, instantiated with the ChatGPT) evaluates outputs, proposes corrections, and assigns quality scores

modules.name: Traffic-control imitation fine-tuning
modules.scope_reason: LoRA updates model parameters from prompt/action interaction logs to specialize traffic-control decisions; R2 places parameter-updating policy training on the LLM side.

evidence.quote: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) [16] inserts low-rank adapters into selected layers and updates parameters, reducing computation and storage while preserving the base model.

modules.name: Critic-corrected score-ranking fine-tuning
modules.scope_reason: Critic-corrected trajectories and scores train the policy to improve later traffic-control actions from workflow feedback. R2 places parameter updates on the LLM side.

evidence.quote: Training alternates among interaction data collection, criticguided correction, and updates of the LLM-Agent using Lscore .

process_validity.quote: Hallucination is defined as context-incoherent, repetitive, or constraint-violating outputs at the decision step. The metric is computed as the fraction of interactions that exhibit any such symptoms.

task_performance.quote: HeraldLight achieves a 20.03% reduction in average travel time relative to SOTA method.
